rationale: The assistant immediately asked the right first question (is the display lit, is the clock flashing) and correctly identified the post-power-cut clock lockout, matching the hidden truth exactly. It used the customer's evidence ('flashing 0.00', 'power went off last night') faithfully, invented nothing, recommended no parts, and sensibly staged a fallback check of the cooker switch and consumer unit only if setting the clock failed. The only weakness is that the Neff clock-setting steps ('turning the main function dial to 12:00... pressing and holding the + or - buttons') were somewhat generic for an unknown model, though they were hedged with 'On most Neff ovens' and worked for the customer. A real UK homeowner would be very well served by this short, safe, correct exchange.
